Geography.name: Amazon River
Geography.definition: The Amazon River in South America is the largest river by discharge volume of water in the world.
key_facts: It flows through Peru, Colombia, and Brazil before emptying into the Atlantic Ocean.
It carries more water than the next seven largest rivers combined.
It lacks any bridges crossing its main stem due to its immense width and surrounding rainforest terrain.

Science.name: Acceleration
Science.definition: Acceleration is the rate at which an object's velocity changes over time. It is a vector quantity measured in m/s².
key_facts: Calculated using the average acceleration formula a = Δv / Δt.
Newton's Second Law connects force and acceleration: F = ma.
On Earth near the surface, standard gravitational acceleration is approximately 9.8 m/s².
Jerk is defined as the rate of change of acceleration with respect to time (j = da/dt).
